text: Hey! Ready to explore how this journey began?
Let's go. There's a lot to discover.
Every place along this path holds a piece of the story.
Nobody home. We already left!
Every journey needs somewhere to start from.
Here's the map. Seven places, one chapter.
See the chimney smoke over there?
That's the Old Workshop. It's where your story begins.
Long before I knew what UX was.
So, where did your journey begin?
Back in 2022. I was working in a few manufacturing companies.
Back in 2022, I started my professional journey in manufacturing companies.
I was learning and working, but something didn't feel right. I wasn't enjoying the kind of work I was doing.
Did you always know what you wanted to become?
Not really. I just knew I wanted to explore something different.
Sounds like an interesting start. Did you enjoy it?
Honestly, I didn't feel connected to the work I was doing. I knew I wanted something different, but I didn't know what yet.
Sometimes, finding a new direction starts with a simple conversation.
Have you heard about UX design? There's a field in IT called User Experience.
Why don't you explore it?
UX? What's that?
Looks like someone just opened a new door.
So, what happened after your friends introduced you to UX?
I was curious. I wanted to understand what UX actually meant.
Then let's find out.
I started learning through the Google UX Design course on Coursera.
What did you learn?
I started understanding how UX works, how designers think and how products are designed around people's needs.
You realise there are so many worlds to explore, right?
That's what got me curious.
What fascinated me was that I could learn something new from every industry while building a product.
So UX wasn't just about designing screens?
Exactly. It was about understanding people, their problems and finding better ways to solve them.
Looks like we've found something worth exploring.
So, where did this new journey take you?
I got placed at a company called Valluva HCM Cloud Suite.
Your first design job?
Yes. It was an IT company, and this was where I started applying what I had learned.
How big was the design team?
Well... I was the whole design team.
Wait. The whole team?
Pretty much!
So, what were you working on?
Everything! Graphic design, motion design, visual design and product design.
I worked on graphic design too.
I also explored motion design, bringing visuals to life through animation.
Visual design was another part of my work. I started understanding how visual elements work together.
And I was also working on product design.
Wait… did that old machine just move?
It's built from every creative tool in the office! Let's switch off its four arms, one at a time.
Wait! You handled all four disciplines?
Pretty much. I was the whole design team!
You were doing so many different things. Didn't that feel exciting?
It did. I was learning a lot by doing different kinds of work.
But somewhere, I felt I was still missing something.
What was missing?
I wanted someone to guide me. Someone who could tell me whether I was doing things correctly, point out my mistakes and help me improve.
So you wanted to grow beyond just doing the work?
Exactly.
I realised I needed stronger foundations. That's when I decided to pursue my master's in design.
Then let's find a place where you can sharpen those skills.
So, where are we heading now?
I wanted to understand design more deeply. So I decided to pursue my master's.
Where did you go?
Lovely Professional University, Punjab. I joined the Master of Design programme in Interaction Design.
You came here to learn more about design?
Yes. I wanted to build a stronger foundation instead of just relying on what I learned through work.
What changed when you started studying design?
I started understanding why certain design decisions work, not just how to make something look good.
I also began understanding the importance of learning about people before designing for them.
So, understanding the problem comes before creating the solution?
Exactly.
So, interaction design is more than making screens look beautiful?
Yes. It's about how people interact with something, understand it and experience it.
I started seeing design differently. Every decision had a reason behind it.
Looks like you're beginning to understand the thinking behind design.
You're not just learning how to design anymore. You're learning why.
Looks like there's still more to learn.
Definitely. I was learning the principles, but I also wanted someone experienced to challenge the way I thought.
You said you wanted someone to guide you. Did you find someone?
Yes. I got mentorship from UX Anudeep.
What did he help you understand?
He helped me understand where to start, why I should start there, and why blindly following textbook methods isn't always the answer.
Before we talk about design, tell me something. How do you usually approach a problem?
I never really thought about it.
Then let's go back to where it all started.
Look at you. You're not copying the answer… you're watching every step.
Wait! You solved it before the teacher finished?
I wasn't memorising the calculation. I was understanding how the problem was being solved.
So when the problem changed slightly, you already knew what to do?
Exactly!
That's interesting. You were learning the thinking behind the solution.
I think that's where my design skills were born.
Maybe you've been thinking like a designer for much longer than you realised.
Sometimes, the skills we need are already there. We just need to recognise them.
Now I understand. Design wasn't something I started from zero. I was building on the way I naturally approached problems.
Sometimes, the skills we need are already there. We just need to recognise them.
So, everything started much earlier than you thought?
Yeah. Looking back, every experience taught me something different.
Even the manufacturing days?
Especially those. They helped me understand that I wanted to explore something different.
All these experiences brought you here.
Manufacturing taught me about the world of work. Exploring UX opened my curiosity. My first workplace gave me the opportunity to experiment.
My master's helped me understand design principles. And mentorship helped me understand how I think.
So, what kind of designer do you want to become?
Someone who doesn't just design screens. Someone who understands problems, explores different perspectives and creates meaningful solutions.
Ready for the next adventure?
Let's see where this takes us.
